reasoning: Sue admits lifting Grant's glass to recover the private agreement carrying her earlier advice, which gave both direct vessel access and a reason to stop Grant using the file against her. Her final defense says her only visit occurred while the manager poured shared punch in the private room and that she stayed watching. The service record instead says the glass was collected at 7:04 and punch poured in the kitchen at 7:06. That contradiction specifically invents supervision for contact with the poisoned vessel. The bottle was accessible and the glass uncovered; the red/silver scrap supports transfer from the bottle closure without uniquely identifying Chip. Chip is the strongest alternative because he fitted that closure, knew the warning and disputes the treatment date. His insurance discrepancy, however, can cover a separate professional problem. Brie's washed measure also remains possible, but clean retained flavoring weakens her most obvious poisoning route. Sue's false account addresses the actual opportunity more directly than those competing suspicions.
feedback: The voices have useful individual texture: Chip's practical impatience, Monets wage deadline, Frank rearranging a chair and Al needing to call home make them more than job titles. The later admissions and appeals across the table suggest relationships under pressure. Twenty-two speeches per round nevertheless create substantial reading burden, and the repeated pattern of professional secret, denial and emotional address starts to feel assembled. Several characters continue denying documentary details in almost identical defensive shapes. The evidence pages are legible and attractive, especially the bottle and frame comparisons. The registrar and settlement pages read more like a consolidated investigator briefing than naturally discovered files, though their headings make comparison easy. I can construct a fair pre-vote case against Sue using the kitchen pouring record, but physical access is sufficiently broad that it remains an inference rather than exclusion of every rival. No essential attending speaker appears missing; the service manager and technician provide documentary accounts. The offstage dealer and relatives do not confuse the cast, and the emotional stakes generally work.

issues.detail: Several final speeches reiterate flat denials of released records, producing a repeated defensive pattern rather than varied responses under pressure.
issues.suggested_fix: Vary one or two innocent responses into partial admissions or specific explanations while preserving their factual clues.

issues.detail: Each full round requires twenty-two substantial speeches; the final method evidence adds six dense pages before another full round.
issues.suggested_fix: Shorten repeated logistics in the final speeches and retain each character's decisive factual claim and strongest personal beat.

issues.detail: The accusation rests heavily on a pouring-location contradiction, while many suspects still have unobserved access and the physical scrap has no unique match.
issues.suggested_fix: Keep the service timeline visually easy to revisit at voting, so the false supervised visit is assessable without relying on memory.
